title: Staging Bench Entitlements Matrix for Hardware Procurement Orders
content:
What the staging bench does to the units of a Hardware Procurement order before they leave belongs to the order type. The matrix lists each preparation entitlement for every order type.

| Entitlement | Accessory & Peripheral Order | Standard Endpoint Order | Staged Endpoint Order | Network Equipment Order | Server & Storage Build Order | Special-Order Equipment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Units asset-tagged and recorded in the client's inventory before delivery | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | No |
| Serial numbers recorded against the client's asset register | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Devices registered for Windows Autopilot | No | No | Yes | No | No | No |
| Firmware updated to the current supported release before shipment | No | No | No | Yes | Yes | No |
| Hours of burn-in testing before shipment | 0 | 0 | 4 | 8 | 24 | 0 |
| Manufacturer warranty registered in the client's name | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Model checked against the manufacturer's end-of-life schedule before quoting | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Signed configuration sheet needed before staging starts | No | No | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Onsite installation part of the order | No | No | No | No | No | No |

## Notes

- Onsite installation is never part of a Hardware Procurement order under any order type; installation is otherwise work done under a ClearPath agreement, a TimeBank block or a project.
- Windows Autopilot registration is an entitlement of the Staged Endpoint Order only.
- Burn-in is stated in hours: a Server & Storage Build Order is burned in for 24 hours, a Network Equipment Order for 8, a Staged Endpoint Order for 4.
